document_title: Alaska's SNAP Bill Reads a Year That Opened Thursday
post_copy:
Alaska's SNAP payment error rate ran 57, 60.4, 24.7 and 23 percent from 2022 to 2025.

All four clear 10 percent, where Public Law 119-21 has a state pay 15 percent of benefit costs. The 2025 rate was the nation's highest and pushed Alaska's share to fiscal 2029. Fiscal 2026's unpublished rate decides whether that becomes fiscal 2030.

From fiscal 2029 that share reads the rate from three fiscal years earlier. Fiscal 2030's share reads fiscal 2027 either way. The state's fix for what it calls "COBOL on a mainframe" is scheduled for 2028. Fiscal 2027 opened October 1st, the day Alaska's share of running SNAP went from 50 to 75 percent.

Steel instruments read the law's shares and Alaska's record, then the state's system, staffing and 2028 fix.

With fiscal 2027 already counting, what should Alaska change in how it decides SNAP cases before 2028?

#AlaskaSNAP #SNAPErrorRate #AKBudget

slides.headline: Alaska's SNAP bill reads a year that opened Thursday.

slides.kicker: THE LAW READS THREE YEARS BACK
slides.headline: Fiscal 2027 is read either way.
slides.body: From fiscal 2029, a state's share uses its error rate from three fiscal years before. Fiscal 2030 reads fiscal 2027, opened October 1st, whichever start applies.

slides.headline: The first share moved on Thursday.
slides.body: Washington's share of SNAP administration fell from 50 to 25 percent, so Alaska now pays 75. Legislative Finance estimates about $6.6 million more a year. The Anchorage Daily News reported nearly $11 million.

slides.headline: The second share is a staircase.
slides.body: Under 6 percent, a state pays none of the benefit cost. At 10 or more, it pays 15 percent.
labels: AT THE TOP STEP, ALASKA COULD OWE MORE THAN $42 MILLION A YEAR, ADN REPORTED

slides.kicker: ALASKA'S SNAP PAYMENT ERROR RATE, BY FEDERAL FISCAL YEAR
slides.headline: The record, against the statute's lines.
slides.body: Alaska's 2025 rate, times 1.5, cleared 20 percent, which moved its start to fiscal 2029. Clear it again in 2026 and the start moves to 2030.
labels: LEGISLATIVE FINANCE FOR 2022 TO 2024, ADN FOR 2025

slides.kicker: THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, IN ITS OWN WORDS
slides.headline: "COBOL on a mainframe."
slides.body: How the state describes EIS, its legacy eligibility system. ARIES, the newer one, holds only MAGI Medicaid.

slides.headline: 218 of 332 positions filled.
slides.body: The yearly average left 34.3 percent vacant. "During periods when Alaska had significant workload backlogs, that had a larger impact on the state's error rate," the Department of Health wrote.
labels: ONE SLOT PER POSITION, CARDS IN READING ORDER

slides.headline: The fix is scheduled for 2028.
slides.body: Milestone 2, estimated at $20 million, began in October 2025. Milestone 2.5, estimated at $5 million, would move SNAP data off the mainframe. The Department says the biggest gains wait for full modernization.

slides.headline: Save this for the day fiscal 2026's rate is published.

editor_notes_for_email: Public Law 119-21 sets each state's SNAP benefit share from its error rate three fiscal years earlier. The deck reads that to mean fiscal 2030's share rests on fiscal 2027, which opened October 1st, the same day Alaska's share of administrative costs went from 50 to 75 percent. It sets Alaska's published rates (57, 60.4, 24.7 and 23 percent) against the statute's tiers, then shows the state's own "COBOL on a mainframe" description, 218 of 332 eligibility technician positions filled in state fiscal 2025, and modernization scheduled for 2028. It never states or implies fiscal 2026's unpublished rate or whether Alaska's start moves to 2030, never adds the $20 million and $5 million budget estimates together, and never blames workers. The added administrative cost appears as two attributed figures, about $6.6 million a year from Legislative Finance and nearly $11 million from the Anchorage Daily News, left unreconciled because neither source explains the other. This story has no AI angle and none was added, because the only AI lead (a Nava tool) had no fetched link to Alaska.
